1 لَمَجَ , (aor.
لَمُجَ , S, M,) inf. n. لَمْجٌ, (S, K,) He ate: or he ate with the extremity of the mouth: (M:) or he ate with the extremities of his mouth: (S, K:) or he took fodder, or dry herbage, with the extremity of his mouth: (T:) AZ says, I know not اللَّمْج except as the act of asses, and it is like اللَّمْس, [probably a mistake for اللَّهْس, or its syn. اللَّحْس,] or signifies more than this latter word. (AHn.) ―
-b2- لَمَجَ, inf. n. لَمْجٌ, Inivit feminam. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
